claims.claim_vi: With a proxied record Cloudflare answers DNS queries with an anycast IP address instead of the origin address and reverse-proxies the traffic, caching content close to users.
claims.section: How Cloudflare works; Cloudflare as a reverse proxy
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone; not tested.

claims.claim_vi: Anycast announces the same IP address from data centers worldwide so each request is routed to a nearby data center.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone; not tested.

claims.claim_vi: Without Tiered Cache, an edge data center that misses must contact the origin; Tiered Cache, a configurable topology, divides data centers into lower and upper tiers so that a lower tier asks an upper tier and only the upper tier asks the origin, reducing origin requests and connections.
claims.verified_by: Read; the nginx experiment showed edge B missing and the regional tier hitting, with the origin counting one request for the image.

claims.claim_vi: The 1.1.1.1 resolver does not send EDNS Client Subnet, so authoritative servers do not receive client IP information from it.
claims.section: Does 1.1.1.1 send EDNS Client Subnet header?

claims.claim_vi: There are private caches (browser) and shared caches; CDNs and reverse proxies are managed shared caches; private restricts storage to private caches; personalized content in a shared cache can leak to other users.
claims.verified_by: Read; in the experiment a response marked private, no-store was never stored at either tier and reached the origin twice.

design_notes_vi: Hai chặng: bốn bước tìm địa chỉ (có cả cách chọn bằng DNS và anycast), ba thẻ tầng bộ đệm nối bằng mũi tên, ba ghi chú kết quả thử. Vẽ bằng scripts/figures.
source_deviations: Source says the CDN load balancer picks the edge from the user's IP address and ISP; the lesson notes that a DNS-based choice sees the resolver's address unless the resolver sends EDNS Client Subnet, and adds anycast as a second way, as Cloudflare documents it.
Source names edge, regional and central servers before the origin; the lesson keeps two tiers and states, from the Cloudflare docs, that only the upper tier contacts the origin.

Source says dynamic content is cached as edge computing results; the lesson does not cover edge computing and adds that Cache-Control from the origin decides what a shared cache may keep, tested with a private, no-store page.
The tiered path (edge, regional, origin) is presented as an optional configuration, as in the Cloudflare docs; without it an edge goes straight to the origin.
